gloss: to receive; to eat/drink (humble); to have someone do (humble auxiliary)

definitions.explanation: Humble form of もらう, used when receiving from someone of higher status.
Humble form of 食べる and 飲む.
Used after て-form to express having someone of higher status do something for you.

examples.english: Thank you for the meal. (said before eating)

notes:
いただく is one of the most versatile humble verbs in Japanese, with three main uses.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: ⟦{他動詞|たどうし}→他動詞：10418_tadoushi⟧ (transitive)
- No standard intransitive pair
- Pattern: [noun]⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧いただく

KEIGO TYPE:
⟦{謙譲語|けんじょうご}→謙譲語：15869_kenjougo⟧ (humble language). Lowers the speaker relative to the listener or the person being discussed.

FUNCTIONS:
1. Humble form of ⟦もらう→もらう：00520_morau⟧ (to receive): ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧から⟦いただいた→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧
2. Humble form of ⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧/⟦{飲|の}む→飲む：00322_nomu⟧ (to eat/drink): おいしくいただきました
3. Auxiliary after て-form (polite request/favor): ⟦{教|おし}えて→教える：00526_oshieru⟧いただけますか

COMMON PATTERNS:
- いただきます: said before meals (lit. "I humbly receive")
- 〜ていただく: to have someone (of higher status) do something for you
- 〜ていただけますか: Could you please...? (very polite request)
- 〜ていただけませんか: Would you mind...? (even more polite)

HONORIFIC COUNTERPARTS:
- ⟦くださる→くださる：01305_kudasaru⟧: honorific for giving (the giver is elevated)
- ⟦{召|め}し{上|あ}がる→召し上がる：01310_meshiagaru⟧: honorific for eating/drinking
